descriptionChirho: A staff or walking stick used for support -- a physical rod carried by hand for walking, leaning, or as a symbol of authority and trust. Used literally of Gideon's staff that touched the offering (Judg 6:21), Elisha's staff sent with Gehazi (2 Kgs 4:29,31), the staff of a recovering injured man (Ex 21:19), and elderly men's staffs in the eschatological age (Zech 8:4). Used metaphorically for political reliance: 'the staff of this crushed reed, Egypt' (2 Kgs 18:21; Isa 36:6; Ezek 29:6). Also 'your rod and your staff comfort me' (Ps 23:4) and the leaders' staffs digging a well (Num 21:18). Multilingual glosses: arb Aasa/Aukkaz, deu Stab/Stecken, fra baton/soutien, hin lathi/chhari (stick/rod), kor jipangi (staff), spa baston/cayado.
